Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: The new independent validation for H247 does not support a scientifically meaningful association between feature_029 level 1 versus level 0 and stronger dependency on outcome_015. Because the registered direction is -1, a positive signed estimate corresponds to a more negative, stronger-dependency score in the exposed group. The discovery estimate R189 was +0.02524 with 95% interval [-0.00025, 0.05073], so it was borderline and not interval-exclusive. First, I register reversed versions of H246 and H249. For outcome_005, H246 (feature_029 level 1 versus level 0) had a discovery contrast favoring weaker dependency in the exposed group, with signed estimate about +0.032 in the reverse direction and an interval roughly 0.005 to 0.060. This point estimate is above the approximate 10% clinical scale for outcomes with mean near -0.25. H249 (feature_035 level 1 versus level 0) also favors weaker dependency in the exposed group, reverse signed estimate about +0.029 with interval roughly 0.001 to 0.056, again near or above the practical threshold. Both have low prevalence and are exposed to multiplicity, so the scientifically useful action is to register the reverse hypothesis explicitly and allow independent validation before treating them as supported. Second, I register feature_054 level_002 versus level_001 for ten untested low-dispersion core outcomes: outcome_012, outcome_002, outcome_015, outcome_007, outcome_013, outcome_008, outcome_004, outcome_009, outcome_010, and outcome_003. Level counts are adequate and these outcomes have practical absolute thresholds near 0.025 to 0.028. The registered direction is -1, so a positive signed estimate would mean level_002 has a more negative, stronger dependency score than level_001. There is no strong prior direction, so anticipated directions are uncertain. For acceptance, an interval-exclusive effect at or near the 10% scale would be needed, preferably followed by validation for any low-prevalence or borderline candidate. These analyses remain observational and dataset-specific and do not establish causality or generalizability.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using

comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The newly delivered panel completes the feature_054 level_002 versus level_001 main-effect screen. The registered direction is -1, so positive signed estimates correspond to level_002 having a more negative, stronger CRISPR dependency score. None of these comparisons supports a scientifically meaningful stronger-dependency difference. For the low-dispersion outcomes with mean near -0.25, a 10% clinical scale corresponds to roughly 0.025 absolute dependency-score units; for outcome_001 it is about 0.042 and for outcome_006 about 0.0175, though that outcome is higher variance. The largest new point estimate for the registered direction is H258 at +0.0145; H259 and H260 are about +0.013, H262 about +0.008, and all other supportive or opposite-sign estimates are smaller or not in the registered direction. Most intervals include zero, and even those with upper bounds above the approximate clinical threshold are point estimates well below it and therefore not interval-exclusive clinically meaningful effects. H13 is opposite to the registered direction and has a magnitude below the larger outcome_001 threshold; H14 is essentially null. There are no apparent validity problems: all comparison cells are adequate, exposure is a measured nominal predictor, and the analyses are simple mean contrasts. The main competing explanations remain noise, multiplicity across many correlated outcomes and predictors, and possible residual confounding. I therefore reject and close all twelve claims as dataset-specific negative comparisons. I do not request validation for any new null result. The only informative voluntary validation now is H253, an active reverse low-prevalence candidate with the strongest current discovery interval for outcome_005; independent validation is needed before treating it as supported because related low-prevalence reverse candidates have failed validation.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

record.narrative: The delivered panel completes the feature_063 level_002 versus level_001 main-effect screen across the remaining outcomes. The registered direction is -1, so a positive signed estimate means level_002 has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency, than level_001. For the low-dispersion core outcomes with means near -0.25, a 10% practical scale is about 0.025 absolute dependency-score units; outcome_013, outcome_008, and outcome_011 have somewhat larger scales of roughly 0.027, 0.028, and 0.030. None of H265-H275 supports a scientifically meaningful stronger-dependency effect for level_002. Most signed estimates are close to zero and include zero; even where an interval bound exceeds the approximate practical threshold, the point estimate is far below it and the interval is not interval-exclusive for a clinically meaningful effect. For example, H269 outcome_008 has signed estimate +0.0077 with interval -0.0149 to +0.0303, below the practical threshold and not robustly meaningful. H275 outcome_006 is opposite in signed direction and also not interval-exclusive. The only non-null signal is H276 for outcome_014, but the signed estimate is -0.0361 against the registered direction. Converted to the raw exposed-minus-comparator scale, level_002 appears less negative than level_001 by about +0.0361, with raw interval about +0.0022 to +0.0700. That is opposite to the registered hypothesis and, although the raw interval excludes zero and the point estimate is more than 10% of the outcome_014 mean, the lower bound is well below the clinical threshold. Given outcome_014's high variance, the number of prior null or borderline comparisons, and the lack of independent validation, this does not justify accepting a scientifically meaningful feature_063 effect. I therefore reject and close all twelve claims. There are no apparent leakage or cell-size problems: feature_063 is measured with adequate groups, about 712 versus 1190, and the tests are straightforward Welch mean contrasts. Competing explanations include random noise, multiplicity across many correlated outcomes and predictors, and residual confounding. I registered a reverse follow-up proposal linked to H276 only as an unresolved low-priority follow-up, not as an accepted finding. No independent validation is requested now because no existing claim has evidence interval-exclusive at or near the clinical threshold; the next best allocation is completion of the active feature_048 level_001 versus level_003 panel.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: This synthesis closes the due validation response for H247 and clears the remaining low-priority reverse-active claim. H247 tests outcome_015 in feature_029 = 1 versus 0 with the registered direction that exposure has a more negative, stronger CRISPR dependency score. The practical 10% scale for outcome_015 is roughly 0.025 absolute dependency-score units, using the absolute mean magnitude. Discovery R189 was only weakly suggestive: signed estimate +0.0252 with a 95% Welch interval from -0.0003 to +0.0507, so it included null and was not interval-exclusive for a clinically meaningful effect. Independent validation R206 is decisive: signed estimate +0.0056 with interval -0.0338 to +0.0451, far below the practical threshold and compatible with zero or opposite effects. I therefore reject and close H247. This is consistent with the earlier failure of related H252/H253/H254-style low-prevalence binary reverse candidates. I also reassess H290, the reverse follow-up for outcome_014 feature_063 level_002 versus level_001. Its signed discovery estimate is +0.0361, with interval +0.0022 to +0.0700, meaning level_002 appears weaker dependent, i.e. less negative, than level_001. Although the point estimate exceeds the approximate outcome_014 practical scale of about 0.0093, the lower bound is far below that threshold and the interval is not interval-exclusive for a scientifically meaningful difference. With high outcome variance, many prior null or borderline comparisons, and no independent validation, this reverse signal is not supported. I therefore reject and close H290. The active queue is now the high-prevalence feature_048 level_001 versus level_003 main-effect panel, H277 through H288, with 12 claims. H289 for outcome_014 is deferred because outcome_014 is high-variance and the feature_048 evidence context is otherwise weak; feature_048 level_002 remains avoided because the exposed cell is only 25. Overall, the accepted set remains empty. The dataset-specific evidence supports broad negative findings across common binary predictors, high-prevalence nominal contrasts, restricted eligibility contrasts, tested interactions, and validated borderline candidates, but it does not support a causally or generally generalizable predictor effect. Remaining uncertainty includes untested continuous dose-response relationships, rare categorical levels, higher-order interactions, residual confounding, and replication in external cohorts. The most informative next step is to analyze the active feature_048 panel and apply the same criterion: accept only interval-exclusive effects near or above the outcome-specific 10% practical scale, preferably with independent validation. If that panel is null, the investigation should be interpreted as a comprehensive negative screen of the prespecified categorical predictor space rather than evidence of causal absence.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

record.narrative: No assessments are due and the accepted set remains empty. The active priority queue still contains H277-H288, the feature_048 level_001 versus level_003 main-effect panel. Those claims should be analyzed first unless additional capacity exists. To prepare the next high-value screen, I registered a focused panel for feature_042, an untested common binary measured predictor with approximately 463 exposed and 1537 comparator observations. The population is the full supplied cohort. The contrast compares feature_042=1 with feature_042=0. Direction -1 encodes the falsifiable hypothesis that feature_042=1 has a more negative, i.e. stronger, CRISPR dependency score than feature_042=0. Anticipated direction is negative if feature_042 marks a permissive or dependency-associated state, but prior evidence in these core outcomes is absent, so the alternatives remain no association, an opposite association, or an association driven by confounding or technical artifacts. I selected 12 lower- or mid-dispersion outcomes to maximize power for detecting a broad clinically meaningful signal; outcome_006 and outcome_014 are not repeated here because H37/H38 already target those high-variance outcomes and remain deferred. For the selected outcomes, a clinically meaningful effect is about 0.025 absolute dependency-score units using a 10% absolute-scale threshold. Acceptance requires an interval-exclusive signed effect at or near that scale, not merely a nominally small effect. These are observational dataset-specific associations and do not establish causality or generalizability.

Iteration 20/25, stage analyze, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The delivered feature_048 level_001 versus level_003 panel has adequate cells, about 409 versus 1566, and uses simple Welch comparisons without obvious leakage or coding problems. The registered direction is -1, so a positive signed estimate indicates stronger dependency in level_001 than in level_003. None of the 12 claims supports the registered clinically meaningful effect. Most signed estimates are small relative to the approximate 10% practical scale and include zero. H277, H280, H281, H282, and H287 have upper bounds that can exceed an outcome-specific 10% absolute scale, but their intervals are not interval-exclusive for a clinically meaningful stronger-dependency effect and cannot be interpreted as robust. H284 is the only interval-exclusive result, but it is opposite to the registered hypothesis: the raw exposed-minus-comparator estimate is about +0.029 for outcome_009, implying weaker rather than stronger dependency for level_001, with a raw interval roughly +0.009 to +0.049. Although the point estimate is near 11% of the absolute outcome mean, the lower bound is well below the practical threshold, and observing one interval-exclusive result among many correlated outcome tests is consistent with multiplicity. I therefore reject and close all due claims. I do not request independent validation because no claim has discovery evidence interval-exclusive in the registered direction at or near the clinically meaningful threshold, and the opposite H284 signal is too uncertain and post-hoc to justify consuming a validation slot now. H289 is closed as deferred with unresolved status because the feature_048 context is otherwise null and outcome_014 is high variance.

Iteration 20/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative:
The due validation response concerns H253, the reverse-claim that feature_029 = 1 is associated with a higher, i.e. less negative, outcome_005 CRISPR dependency score than feature_029 = 0. Because the claim direction is +1, the displayed intervals are already signed to the weaker-dependency hypothesis. Outcome_005 has an absolute mean magnitude of approximately 0.250, so a 10% practical difference corresponds to roughly 0.025 absolute dependency-score units. Discovery evidence R188 was only nominally suggestive in the claimed direction: signed estimate +0.0324, 95% interval +0.0045 to +0.0604. The upper bound can exceed the practical threshold, but the lower bound is only about 1.8% of the absolute mean and therefore does not establish an interval-exclusive clinically meaningful difference. Independent validation R219 is decisive against the claim: signed estimate +0.0163, independent interval -0.0203 to +0.0529. This includes zero, includes clinically negligible values, and includes the opposite direction. I therefore reject and close H253. This is the final validated reversal from the earlier low-prevalence feature_029/feature_007/feature_035 candidate family; it confirms that nominally interval-exclusive but borderline discovery signals are not reliable enough to accept without an interval that also excludes subthreshold effects.

Current scientific synthesis: the accepted set remains empty because no tested predictor-outcome comparison has evidence for an interval-exclusive association at or above the outcome-specific 10% practical scale. The dataset-specific evidence is broadly negative for common binary measured predictors and high-prevalence categorical contrasts. Main-effect contrasts for feature_002, feature_034, and feature_060 were negative across the screened mid-dispersion outcomes. Subsequent panels for feature_045, feature_008, feature_047, feature_021, feature_032, feature_054, feature_055, feature_063, and feature_048 level_001 versus level_003 were also null for the registered hypotheses, with most signed estimates well below practical scale and intervals including null. The only interval-exclusive feature_048 result was opposite to the registered stronger-dependency hypothesis in outcome_009, but its lower bound remained below the practical threshold and multiplicity made it unsuitable for acceptance or validation. Tested interactions, including those stratified by feature_010, feature_015, and feature_051, did not produce robust subgroup-specific associations.

Supported conclusions are therefore mainly negative and bounded: within this supplied dataset, the analyzed measured predictors and tested subgroups do not show scientifically meaningful differences in the screened CRISPR dependency outcomes under the stated practical threshold. This should not be interpreted as proof of causal absence, because the screen is observational, multiple, dependent on the supplied labels and coding, and not exhaustive of the predictor or outcome space.

Unresolved uncertainty remains for the active feature_042 main-effect panel H291 through H302, the high-variance outcomes outcome_006 and outcome_014 where power is limited, rare categorical levels deliberately avoided because of small cells, untested continuous dose-response relationships, and higher-order interactions. External generalizability and biological interpretation also remain unknown.

The most informative next analysis is to complete the active feature_042 panel and apply the same acceptance rule: accept only an interval-exclusive signed effect at or near the outcome-specific 10% practical scale, preferably with independent validation for borderline or high-impact findings. If feature_042 is null, the investigation should move either to a small pre-specified follow-up panel for remaining high-prevalence categorical predictors, such as feature_028 or feature_036, or to close the broad univariate categorical screen and interpret the accumulated result as a negative discovery screen rather than a search for marginal borderline effects.

record.narrative: The feature_042 binary contrast H291-H302 is a well-powered main-effect screen: exposed level 1 has n=463 and comparator level 0 has n=1537, satisfying the cell-count rule. All analyses are simple Welch exposed-minus-comparator contrasts within the full eligible population, with no subgroup conditioning or eligibility filtering, so the main methodological concerns are multiplicity and the practical threshold rather than leakage or coding errors. The claims were registered with direction -1, so positive signed estimates would support stronger dependency (more negative outcome) among feature_042=1 relative to feature_042=0. For the core outcomes, a 10% practical difference corresponds to roughly 0.025 absolute dependency-score units because the absolute outcome means are near -0.25; for outcome_008 it is about 0.028. Most signed estimates are small, interval-inclusive, or in the opposite direction. H294, H293, H301, H297, H298, and H300 are essentially null. H291, H292, H295, H299, and H302 are negative relative to the registered stronger-dependency hypothesis, and H291/H292/H295/H299 intervals include zero. H302 is interval-exclusive but opposite: signed estimate -0.0295, interval -0.0536 to -0.0055, implying weaker rather than stronger dependency in feature_042=1 for outcome_008. Although the point magnitude is near 10% of the absolute mean, this contradicts the registered claim and does not justify acceptance. H296 is the only interval-exclusive result in the registered direction: signed estimate +0.0195, interval +0.0010 to +0.0380. It is close to the practical threshold but not robust enough to accept: the point estimate is below the 10% scale, the lower bound is near zero, and the upper bound alone does not establish a clinically meaningful interval-exclusive difference. Given the twelve correlated outcome tests within this panel, and the broader screen involving hundreds of comparisons, one borderline zero-exclusive result is compatible with multiplicity. I therefore reject all twelve registered feature_042 stronger-dependency claims and close the panel. I do not request independent validation because no claim has discovery evidence that is interval-exclusive at or near the clinically meaningful threshold in the registered direction; validating a near-threshold opposite or borderline signal would not change the conclusion that this dataset-specific screen remains negative. All statements remain observational, dataset-specific, and noncausal.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative:
This panel tests two nominal categorical contrasts: feature_028 level_001 versus level_003 and feature_036 level_001 versus level_002, across twelve low- to mid-dispersion CRISPR dependency outcomes. The contrasts are simple full-population Welch comparisons with no eligibility filters or subgroup conditioning, so there is no obvious leakage from post-selection conditioning. The nominal level coding is appropriate because the comparisons use explicit labels rather than numeric recodes. The main threats are multiplicity, marginal-confounding bias, and the practical-threshold rule rather than coding error. The exposed categories are small but adequate: n=147 for feature_028 level_001 and n=246 for feature_036 level_001, against n=1509 comparator cells, so the 20-per-cell rule is satisfied.

For direction -1, positive signed estimates support the registered hypothesis of stronger dependency, i.e. a more negative raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast. H303 is the only interval-exclusive result in the registered direction: signed estimate +0.0357, 95% interval +0.0070 to +0.0644. In raw terms this corresponds approximately to exposed-minus-comparator -0.0644 to -0.0070. The point magnitude is about 14% of the absolute outcome_012 mean and could be clinically relevant, but the lower bound is only about 3% of the absolute mean. Therefore the interval remains compatible with a clinically negligible difference. By the pre-specified acceptance standard, that is not enough to accept H303. It also does not justify rejection of the possibility of a real effect, because the upper interval is large and the registered direction is supported. I leave H303 unresolved and request independent validation, because it is the sole panel result that could plausibly change the otherwise negative screen. Independent validation will be accepted only if it supports the same direction and also makes the practical-scale conclusion much more robust; if the validation interval is near-threshold or compatible with negligible effects, H303 should be rejected and closed.

The remaining feature_028 outcomes are inconsistent with H303 and do not support accepting a feature_028 level_001 stronger-dependency signal. H304 is interval-exclusive but opposite to the registered claim: signed -0.0311, interval -0.0610 to -0.0012, implying raw weaker dependency for feature_028 level_001 in outcome_005. That is hypothesis-generating only, not support for H304, and its lower bound is also very close to zero. H305, H306, H307, and H308 are null or interval-inclusive, with several estimates pointing in the opposite direction. This pattern makes H303 less credible as a robust family effect, but it still warrants one validation check because it is the only registered-direction zero-exclusive result.

The feature_036 contrasts H309-H314 are uniformly negative for clinically meaningful registered-direction effects. All intervals include zero or clinically negligible values; magnitudes are at most about 0.021 signed units, generally near or below the practical threshold and often opposite to the registered direction. Given 12 highly correlated outcome tests within this panel, and hundreds of comparisons overall, these results are best interpreted as negative for feature_036 level_001 versus level_002. I reject and close H309-H314.

All statements are dataset-specific observational associations. They do not establish causality, biological mechanism, or external generalizability.
